section_provenance: The file carries Major NCD, Mild NCD and Delirium, each with its own A, B, C, D. Extraction is fenced to the MAJOR block only, per D9 (target MAJOR NCD only). Without the fence the parser would silently mix Mild and Delirium criteria into the same letters.
counting_rule: DSM-5-TR requires criteria A through D. Criterion A is met by a decline in AT LEAST ONE cognitive domain, a threshold of one, which sets no counting gate over the domain list. Criterion A's numbered sub-items 1 and 2 are EVIDENCE REQUIREMENTS (informant or clinician concern; documented neuropsychological impairment), not symptom domains, and are not scoreable in a mouse under any vocabulary.
scored_grain_note: Two scored criteria, A and B, per D10. The six cognitive domains below are description text: DSM-5-TR treats them as a defined closed set, but a threshold of one sets no counting gate, so they are components rather than counted items. Recorded per term in the `component` field so the roll-up is auditable, since NCD's current strict universe is dominated by a single motor_coordination bucket of 146 terms and that needs to be visible as perceptual-motor rather than hidden as coverage of Criterion A generally.

items.components_provenance: Paraphrased by the project in DSM5_paraphrased/NCD_criteria.txt. The names below are the construct names that text uses, listed for the component field only.
items.dsm_definition:
Complex attention: keeping attention over time, splitting it between tasks, choosing what to attend to, and speed of processing.
Executive function: planning, making decisions, holding and using information in working memory, using feedback to correct errors, suppressing habitual responses, and switching flexibly between mental sets.
Learning and memory: immediate memory; memory for recent events, tested by free recall, by recall with cues and by recognition; very long-term memory for facts and for one's own life; and learning without awareness (implicit learning).
Language: producing language (naming things, finding words, fluency, grammar and sentence structure) and understanding it.
Perceptual-motor: visual perception, building or copying with visual guidance, coordinating perception with movement, carrying out learned skilled movements (praxis), and recognizing what is perceived (gnosis).
Social cognition: recognizing emotions in others, and understanding the mental states of other people (theory of mind).

items.note: THIS CRITERION IS THE MAJOR VERSUS MILD DISCRIMINATOR, NOT A SEVERITY THRESHOLD. Major and Mild neurocognitive disorder share Criterion A apart from a substantial versus a modest decline: both require acquired cognitive decline in at least one of the six domains. What separates them is THIS criterion. For Major, the deficits GET IN THE WAY of independence in everyday life, so that at the least the person needs help with demanding instrumental activities of daily living, for example handling bills or keeping track of medicines. For Mild, those same activities are KEPT, though they may take more effort or compensating strategies. This spec is fenced to Major per register item D9, so a term admitted here is part of what makes the diagnosis Major rather than Mild. Judge it on interference with independent activity, not on the severity of the cognitive deficit itself, which belongs to Criterion A.

excluded_criteria.C: Not exclusively during delirium. Exclusion criterion, not a symptom.
excluded_criteria.D: Another mental disorder does not account better for the deficits. Exclusion criterion, not a symptom.

worked_examples_provenance: Deliberately empty. See the note in ASD.json.
known_defect_being_fixed: The current NCD taxonomy has no DSM domain structure. Its strict buckets are motor_coordination 146, cognitive_executive 87, neuropathology_progressive 60, social_cognition_empathy 43 and adaptive_functioning 34. Two problems follow. First, neuropathology_progressive is not a DSM Criterion A cognitive domain; it is neuropathology, which under a criterion-anchored design belongs on the mechanism axis and should not be strict-admissible, and it is 60 of the 386 strict terms. Second, cognitive_executive lumps complex attention, executive function, learning and memory, and language into one bucket, so which DSM domain is actually carrying NCD's Criterion A cannot currently be read off the taxonomy at all.
disclosure_required: D12. DSM Criterion A says DECLINE from a previous level of performance, a within-individual longitudinal comparison. MGI genotype-phenotype annotation is a between-genotype DEFICIT relative to wild type. We score DEFICIT where DSM says DECLINE. This substitution must be disclosed prominently wherever an NCD number appears, and it is the single largest construct concession in the project. D11 additionally holds that language is a floor for NCD.
satisfaction_rule: ILLUSTRATIVE. DSM requires decline in ONE OR MORE cognitive domains, a threshold of one, so Criterion A is MET as soon as ANY ONE of the six domains has a strict match. No partial credit denominator across domains. Criterion A's numbered sub-items 1 and 2 are EVIDENCE REQUIREMENTS, never items. Diagnostic gate: A AND B (C and D are exclusions). Breadth denominator is 2 units; see the ID note on non-comparability.
comparability_note: Breadth denominators differ across disorders (ASD 7, SCZ 5, ID 2, NCD 2) AND the units differ in difficulty, because DSM counts enumerated items in ASD and SCZ but accepts a single example in ID and NCD. Report fraction of scored units met alongside the raw count, and never rank disorders on raw breadth.
variant_note: PRODUCTION VARIANT. Identical to NCD.json except that scored units carry a paraphrase of DSM-5-TR's own definitions. Source: DSM-5-TR, Table 1, Neurocognitive Domains (definitional).
reconstruction_note: Three-column table; definitions reconstructed from the left column and verified token by token, NOT contiguous prose.
